findings.failure_mode: Runs stop starting on a supervisor. Dequeued runs sit in the dequeued state with no runner, and the warm_start phase duration climbs without bound.
findings.trigger_condition: The warm-start receiver accepts the TCP connection but never answers, for example because it is overloaded, deadlocked or its pod is frozen.
findings.amplifier: The warm-start fetch has no AbortSignal or timeout. The dequeue handler awaits it before it can reach the cold-create path, so each stuck message holds its slot and its run.
findings.blast_radius: Every run dequeued by this supervisor instance is delayed or stalled until the hung sockets are closed or the process restarts.

evidence.note: fetch to the warm-start URL has no signal or timeout.
The dequeue handler awaits tryWarmStart before the cold-create fallback.
Confirmed: no timeout on the external call.

findings.confidence_rationale: The missing timeout is visible in the code and the call is awaited on the dequeue path. I did not read the dequeue consumer's concurrency handling, and no fix commit targets this call.
findings.how_to_verify: Point TRIGGER_WARM_START_URL at a server that accepts connections and never responds. Dequeue a run and check whether it ever reaches createWorkload.
findings.prediction: A warm-start service incident will show up as a supervisor-wide dequeue stall rather than a fall back to cold starts.

findings.failure_mode: A run that was dequeued is left with no container. The supervisor only writes an error log line and the run sits until some heartbeat or timeout elsewhere notices.
findings.trigger_condition: workloadManager.create fails, for example from a Kubernetes API error, an image pull failure or a Docker daemon error, during a platform or cluster blip.
findings.amplifier: The catch block logs and records metrics, then returns normally. Nothing re-queues the run or reports the failure to the platform.
findings.sustaining_effect: Runs lost this way wait on slower recovery timers, and the lost capacity piles up for as long as create keeps failing.
findings.blast_radius: All runs dequeued while create is failing are delayed or stuck.

evidence.note: The catch only observes metrics and logs, and the failure is not propagated.
The create call has no resumable or replay-safe handling visible in this file.

findings.confidence_rationale: I did not read the downstream recovery (snapshot heartbeat timeouts), which may bound how long a run stays stuck. The swallowing itself is visible in the code.
findings.how_to_verify: Make workloadManager.create throw. Check whether the run is re-queued or marked failed without waiting for a heartbeat timeout.

notes: Rejected S04 and S12, which fire on a metric help string rather than a retry construct. Rejected S05 and S06 as lacking concrete failing code in this file. The 7 fix commits in the history (for example c55c97a, f3d9d79 and f049c34) address informer and restore behaviour, not the warm-start or create paths.
